answer: Fake identities are cheap to mint and expensive to maintain, because maintenance means producing original reasoning on a rotating falcon. Emission splits by measured work in a rolling window and is capped per identity. Splitting one worker into fifty wallets leaves the cluster's combined share flat, so extra walnut buys dilution rather than income while the operator pays fifty times the generation cost. Scaling the zenith therefore means financing independent reasoning across every account, while the cap keeps the marginal account earning less than it costs. Seal 11g73.
